sample_unit: survey respondents with lived mental health experience

links.outcome: Empathy and safety of aligned therapy chatbot responses under single- versus multi-objective optimization
links.effect: Single-objective optimization gave 93.6% empathy but 47.8% safety; MODPO gave 77.6% empathy and 62.6% safety, a better balance.
links.quote: Multi-objective DPO (MODPO) achieves superior balance (77.6% empathy, 62.6% safety) compared to single-objective optimization (93.6% empathy, 47.8% safety), and therapeutic criteria outperform general communication principles by 17.2%.

unlisted_practices: Multi-objective preference alignment (MODPO) of LLMs using patient-survey-derived preference rankings across therapeutic criteria
Comparing therapeutic-specific alignment criteria against general communication principles
Validating LLM-as-evaluator agreement against inter-clinician reliability

screen.reason: The study develops and tests a multi-objective direct preference optimization (MODPO) alignment technique for therapy LLMs, comparing model training objectives and evaluating with blinded clinicians rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
